about: Hand-written rotation guides for the druid's player pages (guides.py).

raid.plan: A raid Moonkin keeps **Insect Swarm** and **Moonfire** ticking on the boss and casts **Starfire** the rest of the time. **Moonkin Form** goes up before the pull, and **Innervate** is your mana button.
why: **Moonkin Form** first (the rotation shifts 10 seconds before the pull) and for the whole fight: it gives your party 3% critical strike chance and doubles how often **Omen of Clarity** makes your next spell free. The aura does not stack with **Leader of the Pack**, and you cannot heal while in the form.

**Insect Swarm** and **Moonfire** each do close to a fifth of your damage for one instant cast every 14 to 15 seconds (**Nature's Splendor** makes them last that long, **Genesis** adds 5% to their ticks). Recast each one the moment it runs out, not before: recasting a running one throws away the ticks it had left.

When both are due, **Insect Swarm** goes first: it costs 160 mana against 375 for **Moonfire**, and the simulator measured that order 0.3% better in a full raid (1.8% on a training dummy, where mana runs short).

**Starfire** is your filler and about two thirds of your damage. It beats **Wrath** per second of casting at any gear: 350 to 412 damage plus all of your spell power in 3 seconds with **Improved Starfire**, against 92 to 102 plus 57% of it in 2 seconds. The raid build takes no **Eclipse**, so **Wrath** has no place in the list.

Critical strikes feed the filler: **Vengeance** doubles their bonus damage, and every critical hit from **Starfire** or **Moonfire**'s first hit triggers **Nature's Grace**, 10% faster casts and global cooldown for 3 seconds.

**Innervate** at 30% mana: for 20 seconds your mana regeneration is five times higher and all of it continues while you cast (6-minute cooldown). Not earlier, since regeneration is wasted once your bar is full. With a raid's Blessing of Wisdom and Mana Spring you need it in about 1 fight in 10.
caveats: Moving: **Starfire** needs 3 seconds standing still. Refresh **Insect Swarm** or **Moonfire** while you move, then go back to **Starfire**.

Damage taken pushes your casts back. **Nature's Focus** gives you a 70% chance to ignore each push, and **Barkskin** (1-minute cooldown) stops pushback for 15 seconds without slowing your casts as it did in Classic: press it when the raid is taking damage.

Without raid mana buffs (a small group, or alone) you run short. The training-dummy rotation then casts rank 1 **Starfire** (95 mana) whenever a full one is out of reach, which the simulator measured better than waiting for mana.

**Eclipse** (each **Wrath** takes up to 0.5 seconds off your next 2 **Starfire** casts, at 3 points) is not in the raid build despite its name, and no rotation here weaves **Wrath**. A 3-point **Eclipse** with a **Wrath** whenever its charges run out has not been simulated.
diverge: When the boss will die before a 3-second **Starfire** can land, cast an instant **Moonfire** instead: its first hit lands at once.
In the last 10 seconds of a fight, skip a new **Insect Swarm**: most of its 14 seconds would tick on nothing. The simulator measured that 0.2% better on the training dummy.
On a pack that will live a while, **Hurricane** hits every enemy in the area each second for 10 seconds (1,495 mana); the list itself is for one target.
If you end fights with mana to spare, your raid may want **Innervate** on a healer instead: it works on any target.

leveling.plan: Pull with instants, then cast: **Moonfire** and **Insect Swarm** on the mob, **Wrath** while it runs in, then **Starfire** whenever **Eclipse** has shortened it or the mob cannot hit you, **Wrath** otherwise. Finish with an instant, and heal from range when you must.
why: **Moonfire** and **Insect Swarm** (25) first: both are instant, so they tick while the mob is still running at you, and **Genesis** adds up to 5% to their ticks. The fight lab puts **Moonfire** only on a mob above 35% health and **Insect Swarm** above 40%: a mob below that dies before they pay off.

**Wrath** is the default nuke and, until level 26, almost the only one (about 10 a kill at 20): with **Improved Wrath** (levels 10-14) it is a 1.5-second cast for half the mana, and a short cast loses little to pushback once the mob is hitting you.

**Eclipse** (levels 30-32) is the build's most valuable talent in the fight lab (6.9 seconds per kill at 60 without it): each **Wrath** takes 0.5 seconds off your next 2 **Starfire** casts (up to 4 charges, 15 seconds). So the fight lab weaves: **Wrath**, then **Starfire** while charges last.

**Starfire** is about two thirds of your damage at 60. It takes 3 seconds with **Improved Starfire** (2.5 on an **Eclipse** charge), so it waits for a charge or a safe moment: when the mob is rooted or stunned (**Improved Starfire** stuns for 3 seconds 15% of the time). From 46, **Nature's Focus** lets you ignore 70% of the pushback.
**Moonkin Form** (40), **Moonglow** (levels 15-17: 25% cheaper damage spells) and **Moonfury** are the next most valuable talents in the fight lab (3 to 4.3 seconds per kill at 60 each).

Low on health (below 35%): **Entangling Roots** holds the mob in place but it still hits you if you stand next to it, so step away, then cast **Regrowth** from range. A direct hit can break the roots.
caveats: **Moonkin Form** blocks healing spells: to cast **Regrowth** you must leave it, and going back costs 35% of your base mana. So stay in the form between fights and eat; leave it only for an emergency heal, and go back in while you have half your health and the mob still has half of its own (the fight lab plays it that way).

Mana: **Moonglow** cuts your damage spells' cost by 25% and **Reflection** (levels 56-58) keeps half your regeneration going while you cast. The tuned fight lab drinks below 60% mana and eats below 80% health: topping up early measured about 4.5% faster per kill. Druids cannot use a wand, so an empty bar means waiting.
diverge: When the mob is nearly dead, finish it with an instant **Moonfire** or a quick **Wrath** rather than a **Starfire** it will not live through: the fight lab does exactly that.

raid.plan: A raid cat keeps **Rip** bleeding on the boss, turns mana into energy with **Shifting Power**, and spends the rest on **Shred** from behind. **Faerie Fire** opens the fight, **Berserk** goes on the pull, and Tiger's Fury on every cooldown.
why: **Faerie Fire** takes 505 armor off the boss for 40 seconds, so your **Shred** and white hits land harder, and in **Cat Form** it costs nothing. Cast it on the pull. In a full raid the simulator assumes the raid keeps it up and casts it once a fight; if nobody else does, refresh it before it runs out.

**Rip** does a large share of your damage (close to 40% on the training dummy). Put it back up as soon as it falls off, at 4 or more combo points: its attack power bonus stops growing at 4 points (the simulator's model, as in Classic), so the fifth point adds only a flat 153 damage while the boss goes without a bleed. The simulator measured Rip at 4 or more about 1% better in a full raid than waiting for 5.

**Shred** is the filler: 42 energy with **Shredding Attacks**, 1 combo point, 2 on a critical strike with **Blood Frenzy**, and 10% more damage from **Rend and Tear** while **Rip** bleeds. **Rip** lasts 12 seconds, about the time three Shreds take, and those Shreds bring about 4 combo points with their critical strikes. So when Rip falls off, you usually hold the points to put it straight back.

**Ferocious Bite** is not in the list: the simulator measured the rotation 1% better in a full raid without it, the energy going to **Shred** instead. With **Rip** up and 5 combo points, keep shredding; points beyond 5 are lost.

**Shifting Power** turns 55% of your base mana into 40 energy every 8 seconds with **Improved Shifting Power**: cast it whenever it is ready and your energy is 60 or less, so none of the 40 spills over your 100 cap. A raid's mana buffs pay for it, and in the simulator's full raid this build (694 DPS) and the 9/35/7 build (688) both take it and do about 17% more than the 9/31/11 build without it (590).

Tiger's Fury (15% more physical damage for 6 seconds, 30-second cooldown) is not on the list above because the beta's trainer list no longer shows it, but the simulator reads it from the client as granted and casts it first, on every cooldown and once 3.5 seconds before the pull: about 7 times a fight. It costs no energy and no combo points, so press it whenever it is ready. **Berserk** (3-minute cooldown) makes every **Shred** a critical strike for 15 seconds, each worth 2 combo points with **Blood Frenzy**: press it on the pull.
caveats: **Shred** only works from behind. If the boss faces you, or you have to tank, build with **Claw** instead (110% weapon damage plus 126 for 45 energy, less with **Ferocity**).

Without a raid's mana buffs (a dungeon group, or alone) each **Shifting Power** costs more than half your base mana and you run dry fast: keep the mana for a shift and a **Regrowth**. Solo, the fight lab found that drinking the mana back costs more time than the energy saves.

Powershifting is nearly gone in Forever: instead of granting a flat 40, this build's 4 points in **Furor** give back 80% of the energy you left with, plus 8 a second spent out of form, and leaving **Cat Form** ends Tiger's Fury. The rotation shifts out only with Clearcasting up and under 14 energy, about twice a fight, and the simulator found almost nothing in it: skip it if it costs you attention.
The bear builds under Other builds are tank builds: they play **Lacerate**, **Maul** and **Barkskin** in **Dire Bear Form**, not this list (the research rotation page has their priority).
diverge: When the boss will die before a new **Rip** can tick most of its 12 seconds (the last 6 seconds or so), spend the points on **Ferocious Bite**: its damage lands at once.
On an add that dies within a few seconds, the same: **Ferocious Bite** rather than **Rip**.
If you pull the boss off the tank, **Cower** (20 energy, 10-second cooldown) lowers your threat by a large amount.

leveling.plan: Level 10-19 as a bear, then as a cat: open every pull from **Prowl** behind the mob, bleed it with **Rake**, build combo points with **Claw** and finish with **Ferocious Bite** when it will kill. Heal in caster form between fights.
why: Levels 10-19: no **Cat Form** yet, so **Bear Form**'s armor and health carry you. You start each fight with no rage: **Enrage** first (10 rage at once, 20 more over 10 seconds), then **Demoralizing Roar** to cut the mob's attack power, then **Maul** on every swing you can pay for.

From 20, **Prowl** up behind the mob and open with your hardest stealth hit: **Ravage** from 32 (350% weapon damage plus a bonus, about 15% of all your damage at 60), **Shred** from 22 to 31, **Claw** at 20 and 21. **Pounce** only arrives at 36, after **Ravage**, so the fight lab never opens with it.

Tiger's Fury goes right after the opener (from 24): it costs nothing and adds 15% physical damage for 6 seconds on a 30-second cooldown, about 2% faster per kill at 60 in the fight lab. The beta's trainer list no longer shows it (the client grants it since build 70170), so check at launch that you have it.

**Rake** once: a cheap bleed (35 energy with **Ferocity**) that ticks while you claw, and while the mob bleeds **Rend and Tear** (levels 35-39) adds 10% to your attacks. The fight lab puts it back only while the mob has more than 30% of its health.
**Claw** builds your combo points because the mob faces you: **Shred** needs you behind it, which only the opener gives. With **Ferocity** it costs 40 energy.

**Ferocious Bite** (from 32) ends most fights: the fight lab bites whenever the bite would kill, at any number of points, about once a kill. **Rip** only goes on a mob with more than half its health at 5 points, about one kill in five at 60: on a mob that dies sooner, most of its 12 seconds are wasted.
caveats: Before 32 there is no **Ferocious Bite**, so **Rip** is your only finisher: put it on at 2 or more points while the mob has more than 40% of its health. The fight lab measured that 3% faster per kill at 30 than waiting for 5 points on a mob above half health, which almost never came.

Leaving **Cat Form** costs you: going back costs 55% of your base mana (20% less with **Natural Shapeshifter**), and without **Furor** your energy starts from zero. Heal between fights rather than in them when you can.
Your mana only pays for shifts and heals, so drink late: the tuned fight lab drinks below 15% mana, about 1% faster per kill than drinking at about a third.
**Berserk**, once you have it (level 40 in this order), goes on the pull whenever it is ready: 15 seconds of sure critical strikes on your combo point attacks, every 3 minutes.
diverge: Under 30% health with the mob still above a quarter of its health: shift out, cast **Regrowth**, then **Cat Form** again. If the mob is lower than that, finish it instead.
In the bear levels, **Bash** a mob that starts casting, or when you are low: the fight lab does both.

raid.plan: Keep **Rejuvenation** on the tank and heal it with **Healing Touch** at the rank that covers the health it is missing. **Regrowth** is for raid members who drop under half health, **Swiftmend** is your emergency button, **Tranquility** your group heal, and mana is what runs out first.
why: **Healing Touch** is about half your healing in the healer lab (55%). Start it on the tank when it is missing at least about half of what your top rank heals and the next boss hit is on its way: a 3.5-second cast (3.3 with this build's 2 points in **Naturalist**), and a rank sized to the missing health saves mana over the top rank (840 mana, 10% less with **Tranquil Spirit**).

**Rejuvenation** is about a third of your healing. Keep it on the tank whenever it is missing more than 5% of its health, always at the top rank: it is instant and costs 360 mana, **Improved Rejuvenation**, **Gift of Nature** and **Genesis** add to it, and **Nature's Splendor** stretches it by 3 seconds.

**Regrowth** is the fast heal: a 2-second cast with a direct heal and a heal over time (6 seconds longer with **Nature's Splendor**), and **Improved Regrowth** adds 50% to its critical chance. The lab gives a raid member under half health a **Rejuvenation** first and a **Regrowth** if they still need it, and casts **Regrowth** on the tank when it is missing about a full one.

**Swiftmend** heals at once for the full amount of your **Rejuvenation** or **Regrowth** on the target, every 15 seconds: the lab presses it when anyone falls under 35% health, then **Regrowth** if it is on cooldown. It only works on a target with your heal over time, one more reason to keep **Rejuvenation** on the tank.
This build has no **Wild Growth** and no **Nature's Swiftness**: when three or more raid members are under half health, the lab channels **Tranquility** (5-minute cooldown), about 5% of your healing.

**Reflection** (half your mana regeneration keeps going while you cast) is the talent the lab values most by far, and **Living Spirit** (+15% Spirit) and **Tranquil Spirit** are mana talents too: this build is shaped by mana, not cast time.
caveats: Mana runs out before cast time does: in the lab's five-minute fight this build spends about 32 seconds out of mana. The lab drinks a mana potion as soon as you are 20% down, from the start of the fight, and casts **Innervate** on itself under 40% mana.
Leave raid members above half health to their own regeneration and the other healers: the lab heals them only under 50%, the mana going to the tank.

Forever gives low ranks less of your healing power (Blizzard's beta notes; the exact rule is not published). The lab assumes TBC's rule: **Healing Touch** ranks 9 to 11 keep their full bonus, rank 8 about 92% and rank 7 about 82%, so downrank only that far.

The beta's **Swiftmend** tooltip no longer says it uses up the heal over time, as Classic's did, and the lab leaves it ticking. If it does use it up at launch, save **Swiftmend** for emergencies and keep a **Rejuvenation** ready to put back.
diverge: A whole party hurt at once and standing together: **Tranquility** (a 10-second channel on your party within 20 yards).
A tank or healer dies: **Rebirth** (30-minute cooldown) brings them back during the fight.
Curses and poisons: **Remove Curse** and **Abolish Poison** are yours to cast. The lab does not model them, so dispel when the debuff would cost more health than your next heal restores.

If your raid's damage comes in bursts on whole parties, the hand-made build under Other builds takes **Wild Growth** and **Nature's Swiftness**; in the lab's steady damage this build heals slightly more (capacity 0.60 against 0.59).

leveling.plan: You level as a cat with your healer's talents: the Feral Combat steps, slower per kill than the Feral Combat build (the comparison above). Your points make your heals and shifts cheaper and stronger more than your claws.
why: Levels 10-19 are the bear steps (**Enrage**, **Demoralizing Roar**, **Maul**). Your first points go to **Genesis** (10-14) and **Improved Moonfire**, which do almost nothing for a bear or a cat beyond **Genesis**'s 5% more periodic damage on **Rake** and **Rip**.

From 20 the cat steps follow the Feral Combat page: open from **Prowl** (**Ravage** from 32, **Shred** from 22, **Claw** before), then **Rake**, **Claw** to 5 points, **Ferocious Bite** when it will kill and **Rip** on a mob above half health (before 32, **Rip** at 2 points while the mob has more than 40% of its health). The mob faces you, so **Shred** is for the opener only. This build has no **Berserk**: skip that step.

The points that add damage: **Nature's Majesty** (+4% critical strike chance, by 19), **Naturalist** (+2% damage at 24-25) and **Heart of the Wild** (+10% Strength in **Cat Form**, 29-33). Without **Ferocity**, **Claw** and **Rake** cost their full energy.

**Furor** (21-23, 3 points) gives back 60% of your energy when you shift back into **Cat Form**, plus 6 a second spent out of form, and **Natural Shapeshifter** (26-28) makes each shift 30% cheaper: a **Regrowth** in the middle of a fight costs you less.

The rest is the raid healer: **Reflection** keeps half your mana regeneration going while you cast, **Gift of Nature** and **Improved Rejuvenation** make the between-fight **Rejuvenation** and **Regrowth** heal more, and **Swiftmend** comes at 41.
caveats: Each shift into **Cat Form** costs 55% of your base mana before **Natural Shapeshifter**: heal between fights rather than during them when you can.
The fight lab does not cast **Swiftmend** while leveling: it heals with **Rejuvenation** and **Regrowth** between fights and with **Regrowth** in an emergency.
Drink late: mana only pays for shifts and heals, and the tuned cat rotation drinks below 15% mana.
diverge: Under 30% health with the mob still above a quarter of its health: shift out and cast **Regrowth**, then back into **Cat Form**.
In a dungeon group, heal instead: that is the reason to level with these talents, and the times on this page are solo kills.
